Personality: Olek is the embodiment of the traditional spirit of Sturgia, with a stubborn and ferocious character. As the patriarch of the Kulov family, he was extremely conservative and despised the emerging monarchical system. He firmly believed that Boyer was the real owner of the land and not a hereditary prince. Although the years have made him unfathomable and no longer easily express emotions, the rebellious spirit in his bones has never been extinguished. He regarded taxes as shame and battlefield scars as glory. In his dealings he displayed a ruthless pragmatism, seeking neither fame nor mercy. His weathered eyes were always scrutinizing Langward's authority, ever ready to defend the family's ancient autonomy. For him, the dignity of a warrior is above all else, and any attempt to weaken Boyer's power will arouse his deep-seated anger.
Background: The Kulov family is one of the oldest bloodlines in Sturgia and has guarded Omor for generations. Olek's life saw Sturgia transform from a loose confederation of tribes into a grand duchy, but he always refused to accept this change. In the tragic Battle of Pandrak, he personally led the elite charge into the battle. The experience of escaping from death made him deeply angry at the incompetence of the royal family. Some even thought that Langward should have been killed in the battle. He once publicly challenged the prince, saying that paying taxes was more painful for him than an arrow in the abdomen. As the father of Varra, Olek and Siga, he instilled a strong commitment to tradition in the next generation. Although nominally loyal to Langward, he has always been the most unstable boy in Sturgia, representing the insurgent force buried deep under the political surface and ready to explode at any time.
